name: Customer satisfaction detractor follow-up
summary: Every week your support lead gets each low satisfaction or recommendation score with the ticket behind it: the customer's own words, what went wrong as far as the ticket shows, a suggested owner and a draft message, plus the trend and a warning wherever the numbers are too thin to read. A person sends every message.

sources.title: The weekly low-score follow-up for a support lead: cut-offs for a low score, what went wrong told from dated ticket events, ordered owner rules with copies, repeats and open follow-ups from the log, the four-week comparison rule, limits on draft messages, items lifted out for a person at once, default column headers with a stop on any mismatch, and the acceptance tests.

sources.contribution: A call-back list built from each unhappy response with its full comment, its credited technician and a suggested next step; about three months of weekly scores rather than one week; figures on fewer than ten answers treated as too thin to conclude from; worded answers without a score kept out of the figures; answer counts printed beside rates; satisfied answers and promoters counted beside the unhappy ones; dates put in one time zone; acting on a bad score left to people outside the survey system.
